# SOP-P1-L2-05 Planned shutdown - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-041, QS-PROC-03, SOP-P1-L2-04

1. Purpose and scope  
1.1 Purpose: Provide a standardized procedure for executing a planned shutdown of the Ring Rolling line to perform preventative maintenance, inspection, and controlled preservation of assets: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03. This procedure aligns with ECN-2026-041 for engineering change acceptance and QS-PROC-03 for quality records. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-04 for normal production stop procedures and handover practices.  
1.2 Scope: Applies to maintenance, operations, and safety personnel responsible for the Ring Rolling line at Plant P1, line P1-L2.

2. Background and rationale  
2.1 Background: Planned shutdowns reduce risk of unexpected failures, allow inspection of critical wear items, and ensure lubrication and heating systems are preserved. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C; this target is used to confirm heater control systems and thermocouple function prior to shutdown preservation actions. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is CFW-LUB-961; use for replenishment and compatibility checks during shutdown servicing.  
2.2 Rationale: Verifying the heater target temperature and correct lubricant ensures that process-critical systems remain within design intent when returned to service, minimizing start-up rejects and equipment stress.

3. Preconditions (required before initiating shutdown)  
3.1 Approved work order and authorization per ECN-2026-041.  
3.2 All affected departments notified in accordance with QS-PROC-03.  
3.3 Operators available to perform safe machine isolation and to provide process history.  
3.4 Lockout/tagout devices and procedure verified; verify handover to maintenance only after isolation.  
3.5 Materials staged for protective storage or removal from process line.

4. Personal protective equipment (PPE)  
4.1 Required PPE: standard plant safety PPE as defined in site safety rules; hot work PPE for heater access; chemical resistant gloves for lubricant handling when required by material safety data sheets. Consult site safety for any additional PPE needs.

5. Shutdown steps (numbered execution flow)  
5.1 Step 1 — Initiate shutdown authorization  
5.1.1 Confirm work order and scope with maintenance supervisor.  
5.1.2 Notify operations, quality, and production planning per QS-PROC-03.  
5.2 Step 2 — Prepare the line for shutdown  
5.2.1 Stop material feed and secure billets per SOP-P1-L2-04.  
5.2.2 Remove or secure loose workpieces to prevent foreign object damage.  
5.3 Step 3 — Isolate power and energy sources  
5.3.1 Follow lockout/tagout procedure and verify isolation points on EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Only authorized personnel may apply tags and locks.  
5.4 Step 4 — Verify heater control and temperature reading  
5.4.1 With isolation in place, bring monitoring systems to the attention of maintenance for verification. Use the control panel to confirm that the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C in the system records and control setpoints. This confirms that thermocouple mapping and control logic are correct prior to any mechanical intervention.  
5.5 Step 5 — Drain and preserve process fluids as required  
5.5.1 For lubrication and hydraulic systems, drain per manufacturer guidance. When replenishing or topping, use lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) CFW-LUB-961 to maintain compatibility in reservoirs that will remain in service after shutdown. Record quantities added in maintenance log.  
5.6 Step 6 — Inspect and tag critical components  
5.6.1 Inspect bearings, rollers, heater elements, and mechanical couplings for wear signatures. Tag any items requiring follow-up with work orders referencing ECN-2026-041 when parts or changes are required.  
5.7 Step 7 — Housekeeping and preservation  
5.7.1 Clean surfaces and apply preservation coating where specified. Seal electrical enclosures and cover exposed sensors if recommended by equipment vendor.  
5.8 Step 8 — Update controls and set safe states  
5.8.1 Place control systems into maintenance mode and log the pre-shutdown setpoints and alarm states. Ensure that operator panels show the preserved state and that alarms are acknowledged in the record.  
5.9 Step 9 — Final verification and handover to maintenance stores or preservation team  
5.9.1 Walkdown by responsible supervisor to confirm tasks complete and records updated. Sign the shutdown checklist.

6. Examples and common findings  
6.1 Example: If the control display does not show 1230 °C for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 when expected, document the discrepancy and escalate to engineering per ECN-2026-041. Do not proceed with heater element work until thermocouple verification is resolved.  
6.2 Example: If lubricant on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 is unknown, tag reservoir as quarantined and replace with CFW-LUB-961 after draining and sampling documented in the record.

7. Records to keep (per QS-PROC-03)  
7.1 Completed shutdown checklist with signatures.  
7.2 Lockout/tagout log and energy isolation verification records.  
7.3 Heater setpoint verification printout or screenshot showing target billet temperature 1230 °C for EQ-P1-L2-IH02.  
7.4 Lubricant usage and replenishment record showing lubricant part number CFW-LUB-961 for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.  
7.5 Inspection findings and follow-up work orders referencing ECN-2026-041 where applicable. All records retained in accordance with QS-PROC-03.

8. Sign-off (required)  
8.1 Operations lead: signature and date.  
8.2 Maintenance supervisor: signature and date.  
8.3 Quality representative: signature and date confirming records conform to QS-PROC-03.  
8.4 Engineering representative: signature and date if deviations require ECN-2026-041 action.

9. References and cross-checks  
9.1 ECN-2026-041 — engineering change directives and approval requirements.  
9.2 QS-PROC-03 — record retention and notification protocols.  
9.3 SOP-P1-L2-04 — production stop and handover procedures.

Notes: Any deviation observed during execution must be recorded and reported immediately. Use examples in section 6 as a guide for escalation.
